pathways.pathway: Qualified watchmaker, authenticator, or dealer partnership
pathways.practical: This is a real way to obtain examined watches. It requires a named organization, a written method, and permission to keep the photographs.
pathways.evidence_in_repository: No agreement, verifier, or data commitment is recorded.

pathways.practical: Direct photography can separate image rights from the authenticity label when the owner grants permission and a qualified person examines the watch.
pathways.evidence_in_repository: No permission and no new photographs are recorded.

pathways.pathway: Counterfeit examples with affirmative independent evidence
pathways.practical: A customs, brand-security, or laboratory record can support a counterfeit label. A suspicious appearance cannot.
pathways.evidence_in_repository: No such record is available. The existing counterfeit folder is a directory label plus a shared JPEG export.

pathways.practical: Usable only when the card states both image rights and an authenticity method that is independent of a model.
sources_checked: Hugging Face listing and synthetic-verdict sets

pathways.practical: A museum or university set can qualify when the object record and the image license are both published.
pathways.note: FAMOS is an institutional authentication set for package microstructures, not watches. Earlier museum endpoints did not yield licensed watch originals.
